newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends up, March at three-week high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends up, March at three-week high.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures rose sharply Tuesday, ending at three-week highs, fueled by commission house and trade buying, floor sources said.
Traders said the market's upturn Monday and Tuesday was a technical correction to last week's slide to seven-week lows.
"The market should not have gone down as much as it did last week," one analyst said.
March futures gained 2.60 cents per lb, to close at 108.20, having traded from 108.65 to 105.90. May climbed 2.50, to 105.85, while spot December jumped 4.65 to 117.75.
Arabica futures saw steady roaster buying throughout the day, traders said, while the recent bout of producer-linked selling appeared to have sudsided.
"There is roaster interest and origins backed away from selling -- they sold what they had to sell," said Hencorp Becstone president Victor Henriquez.
A tight nearby supply situation continued underpin prices, he said, and uncertainty about the size of the 1997/98 Brazilian crop is likely to keep market participants focused on supplies.
Recent forecasts for 1997/98 Brazilian output have ranged widely between 17.8 million and 30 million 60-kgs of coffee versus around 27 million bags in 1996/97.
"The question is, how big is the 1997/98 Brazilian crop?" Henriquez said. "If it is less than 1996/97, with the drawdown in stock levels, tightness we see now is going to be a reality next year."
But other analysts said while spot supply is tight, more coffee is making its way into the market and any upside potential may be limited.
"I think there is enough coffee out there to cap a rally," an analyst said. "The market has risen 5.00 cents in two days. Roaster buying is likely to cool off."

The latest CSCE certified coffee stock report showed gradable stocks rose by 2,000 60-kg bags for the week ended December 6, to 2,321 bags. In addition, another 5,500 bags were certified for delivery sometime between December 6-9, and a further 11,750 bags were reported pending grading in Miami warehouses.
While the stock increase served as a reminder that supply flows from Latin America were picking up, traders noted stockpiles remained extremely low.
Open interest in the December contract, which expires Dec. 18, stood at to 846 lots Monday, the equivalent of more than 200,000 bags of coffee.
Technically, resistance was seen at 109.00 cents, 0.30 cent above today's high. Sell stops were believed well-placed under 102.00 cents, and then toward 100.00 cents ($1).
An estimated 9,888 lots changed hands on Tuesday.
